candidate.mechanism_difference: F6 exposes body position, velocity, mass/inertia and contact state as dynamic variables that feed back into the fluid. F1 uses fixed obstacle topology, F2 uses prescribed cup/receiver motion, F3 uses prescribed sloshing forcing, F4 uses fluid-stream collision, and F5 uses prescribed wave/run-up geometry; none has an independently moving rigid body with coupled response.
candidate.proposal_decision: Mechanism is suitable for a new proposal and is genuinely distinct at the state-space level, but the existing assets support only a bounded structural probe. They do not support Core T1 admission.

blockers: nominal floating mDBC boundary normals are incomplete
no matched transformed-Float1 force-gauge closure exists

observed_integrity.definition_and_solver_truth: The three custom definitions were prepared and their historical solver receipts report code 0, with no excluded particles. This proves execution authenticity for those old probes, not physical acceptance.
observed_integrity.trajectory_schema: Each HDF5 is schema_version 2 with position, velocity, density, pressure, mass, type, mk, valid, particle_id, particle_zone and strictly increasing time.
observed_integrity.identity: All three custom probes retain every initial numerical particle ID through the final frame; mk 22 identifies the single body and mk 22/23 identify the two twin bodies. This is numerical-node identity only; it is not a material-lineage or body-state contract.
observed_integrity.time_axis: Saved cadence is approximately 0.05 s and reaches 99.99% or more of each declared target. The windows are short probes: 0.6 s for entry and 0.8 s for float/twin response.
observed_integrity.density: Historical audits report density ranges 998.61--1009.86 kg/m^3 for the twin, 998.74--1005.17 kg/m^3 for the single floater, and 982.27--1066.30 kg/m^3 for entry; these pass only the broad exploratory sanity range.
observed_integrity.mass: The HDF5 mass array is a particle field and does not bind rigid-body mass or inertia. For example, the floating-box body mass field sums to 11.2 kg while rho_body times declared box volume is 3.072 kg; the heavy body sums to 9.6 kg while the declared value is 7.168 kg. The twin bodies each sum to 9.6 kg while their declared rho_body volumes are 3.072 kg and 4.096 kg. This is a missing closure contract, not evidence that the historical solver run was false.
observed_integrity.boundary: The XML declares a finite tank with bottom/left/right/front/back faces and an open top, but the normalized HDF5 contains no boundary normals, wall-contact/penetration flags, or open-face flux ledger. Excluded_particles=0 does not close those gates.
observed_integrity.event_window: No event definitions or body-level force/torque traces are present. The heavy body is still moving at its 0.600442 s endpoint, and the float/twin body responses have no declared settling or post-impact completion criterion. Therefore the historical windows are not complete event windows.

must_pass_before_any_future_runtime_auth: Parse a fresh F6 Definition and bind hashes for geometry, fluid density, body density, dimensions, center of mass, inertia, initial velocity and tank open/closed faces.
Derive body volume and mass from the declared geometry and rho_body; require an explicit inertia tensor and a body-level identity that is separate from particle IDs.
Validate HDF5 or equivalent output axes: finite arrays, strictly increasing time, declared cadence, complete target window, stable numerical IDs, mk/body mapping, and zero unexplained exclusions.
Require a body-state sidecar with per-body position, linear/angular velocity, force, torque, contact/penetration status, and mass/inertia provenance.
Require boundary-normal completeness and a wall/open-face accounting contract before any mDBC or Chrono interpretation.
Keep event completion separate from trajectory structural integrity; a complete file with an uncensored body event is required for any T1 review.

future_canary_shape.one_case: single free body, no contact, static/units/inertia control
future_canary_shape.one_resolution: one explicitly bound resolution after root review
future_canary_shape.window: long enough to include static balance and a declared no-contact response window

forbidden_reuse_and_actions: Do not count any F6_floating_box, F6_heavy_box_entry, F6_twin_floaters, O6_floating_box, or Test14 artifact toward a Core T1 denominator.
Do not reuse old generated XML, BI4/OBI4, CSV, HDF5, or trajectory as a fresh qualification input; their hashes may be retained only as read-only evidence references.
Do not promote radius-offset zero-normal diagnostics or fixed-box DBC/mDBC force controls to transformed-Float1 F6 evidence.
Do not mix a dynamic Chrono/contact experiment into a fixed-body hydrostatic gate.
Do not launch solver/GPU/queue work, mutate registry/ledger/matrix, or label this proposal T1.
